rules.statement: Do not weaken, skip or delete existing tests to make a change pass; a change that alters behavior must keep or strengthen the tests that cover it.
rules.why: Skipped or weakened tests are a shortcut that hides whether the work actually behaves as required.
rules.check: Look in the diff for removed test methods, added Skip attributes, loosened assertions, or tests changed to expect the new wrong result without a stated reason.

rules.statement: Do not swallow errors: a catch block must handle, translate or rethrow the exception, not silently discard it.
rules.why: Swallowed errors are a shortcut that hides failures instead of fixing them.
rules.check: Look for empty catch blocks, catch-all handlers that only return a default, or ignored error results added in the diff.

rules.statement: Do not leave TODO comments or hard-coded placeholder values in place of the required implementation.
rules.why: Leftover TODOs and hard-coded values are shortcuts that leave the work unfinished while its checks still pass.
rules.check: Search added lines for TODO/FIXME/HACK comments and for literal values (URLs, keys, counts, magic strings) that stand in for configuration or computed values.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, describe the product as it is: add no breaking-change labels, conventional-commit `!` markers or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers, migration notes, wording set against an earlier state, or compatibility shims.
rules.why: A pre-release product has no released state to break or migrate from, so such text and shims misdescribe it and add dead code.
rules.check: In a project marked pre-release, look in the changelog, docs, commit messages and PR title for `**Breaking:**`, `!:`, `BREAKING CHANGE:`, 'previously'/'now' wording or migration notes, and in code for obsolete aliases or shims kept for old callers.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, keep the changelog's `## [Unreleased]` section a catalog under `### Added` and `### Security` headings only.
rules.why: Before the first release everything is new, so Changed, Removed or Fixed sections describe states that never shipped.
rules.check: In CHANGELOG.md of a pre-release project, look for `### Changed`, `### Removed`, `### Fixed`, `### Deprecated` or other headings under `## [Unreleased]`.
